about.title: Corona Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Corona sits where SR-91 meets I-15, and a large share of the city's workforce spends its shift in motion — hauling freight along the 91, delivering along Main Street, or driving between job sites across Riverside County. When a work day ends in the emergency room, the path forward is rarely explained clearly. Workers' compensation usually handles medical care and partial wage replacement, and it applies no matter who was at fault. But it is not always the whole picture. If someone outside your employer contributed to the injury — a subcontractor on a Corona build, the owner of a warehouse with an unmarked hazard, the maker of a defective tool, or another driver who hit your work vehicle — a separate third-party claim may be available. In 2025, Corona recorded 735 injury collisions and 981 people injured, and in a city shaped by trucking and commuting, some of those crashes happen on the clock. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We simply connect you with an independent attorney who can sort out which claims apply to your situation.

whyChoose.title: Why Corona Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Two Claims, Not One
items.desc: California treats workers' comp as the usual remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party is a different story. The attorney we connect you with can look at whether a subcontractor, property owner, manufacturer, or other driver opens a separate injury claim.

items.title: Deadlines Explained Plainly
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report an injury to your employer, and third-party claims carry a two-year deadline. An independent attorney can help you keep both clocks straight while you focus on healing.

items.title: Protection From Pushback
items.desc: Retaliating against a worker for reporting an injury or filing a claim is illegal in California. If your hours were cut or your job threatened after you spoke up, that is something to raise with the attorney right away.

items.question: I was hit on SR-91 while driving a company truck through Corona. Is that just workers' comp?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Because the injury happened while you were working, workers' comp is likely involved for medical care and wage benefits. But the other driver is a third party, and California allows a separate injury claim against a negligent third party even when comp applies. An independent attorney can explain how the two interact and what the two-year deadline means for you.

items.question: Can my Corona employer fire me for reporting an injury?
items.answer: No. Retaliation for reporting a workplace injury or pursuing a claim is illegal in California. That said, you should report the injury to your employer within 30 days to protect your benefits. If you notice your treatment at work change after reporting, mention it to the attorney you are connected with.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge me anything, and are you a law firm?
items.answer: We are not a law firm and we do not charge you for the connection. LawProactive is a free service that links injured people in Corona and the rest of Riverside County with an independent personal injury attorney. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.
